Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Caused by Xanthomonas euvesicatoria. Spread by rain splash, contaminated tools, and infected seeds.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halos. Raised scab-like lesions on fruit.
treatment: Apply Copper hydroxide or Copper oxychloride bactericides every 5-7 days.
Add Mancozeb to copper sprays to improve effectiveness.
Remove and destroy infected plant debris.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free certified seeds. Practice crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Pepper__bell___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation, proper spacing for air circulation, and use of certified seeds.

Potato___Early_blight.causes: Caused by the fungus Alternaria solani. Favored by warm temperatures and alternating wet and dry periods.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black circular spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) on older leaves.
treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin fungicides every 7-14 days.
Apply Copper-based fungicides as an alternative.
Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Ensure adequate potassium fertilization to improve plant resistance.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers. Practice 3-year crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Potato___Late_blight.causes: Caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans. Spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked pale green to brown lesions on leaves with white mold on undersides. Rapid collapse of foliage.
treatment: Apply Metalaxyl, Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Cymoxanil fungicides immediately.
Apply every 5-7 days during wet weather.
Destroy infected plant material - do not compost.
Hill up soil around plants to protect tubers from spores.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Use certified seed. Apply preventive fungicides before disease appears.

Potato___healthy.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers, practice crop rotation, and monitor fields regularly.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.causes: Caused by Xanthomonas vesicatoria. Spread through rain splash, contaminated tools, and infected seeds.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown with yellow halos. Raised scab-like spots on fruit.
treatment: Apply Copper hydroxide or Copper oxychloride every 5-7 days.
Combine copper with Mancozeb for improved control.
Remove and destroy infected plant material.
Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds. Hot water seed treatment (52 degrees C for 30 minutes). Crop rotation.

Tomato_Early_blight.causes: Caused by Alternaria solani. Favored by warm temperatures and wet conditions.
Tomato_Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves. Yellow areas surrounding spots. Stem lesions at soil line.
treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin fungicides every 7-10 days.
Remove infected lower leaves.
Stake plants to improve air circulation.
Apply mulch to reduce soil splash.
Tomato_Early_blight.prevention: Crop rotation, proper staking, avoid overhead irrigation, use resistant varieties.

Tomato_Late_blight.causes: Caused by Phytophthora infestans. Spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather.
Tomato_Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked pale green lesions turning brown-black. White mold on leaf undersides in humid conditions. Rapid plant collapse.
treatment: Apply Metalaxyl, Mancozeb, Chlorothalonil, or Cymoxanil immediately.
Spray every 5-7 days during wet weather.
Remove and destroy all infected material - do not compost.
Apply Copper-based fungicides as an alternative.
Tomato_Late_blight.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation. Apply preventive fungicides in high-risk weather.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.causes: Caused by the fungus Passalora fulva. Favored by high humidity (above 85%) and warm temperatures.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches on upper leaf surface with olive-green to brown velvety mold on undersides.
treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Copper fungicides every 7-10 days.
Reduce humidity by improving ventilation in greenhouses.
Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Avoid wetting foliage when irrigating.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Ensure proper plant spacing. Control humidity in greenhouse production.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Caused by the fungus Septoria lycopersici. Spreads through rain splash and infected plant debris.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and light gray centers with tiny black dots inside.
treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Copper fungicides every 7-10 days.
Remove infected lower leaves immediately.
Apply mulch to reduce soil splash.
Stake or cage plants to improve air circulation.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Crop rotation (3 years). Avoid overhead irrigation. Remove crop debris after harvest.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.causes: Caused by Tetranychus urticae mite infestation. Thrives in hot, dry, dusty conditions.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.symptoms: Tiny yellow stippling on upper leaf surface, bronze or silvery discoloration, fine webbing on undersides of leaves.
treatment: Apply Abamectin, Bifenazate, or Spiromesifen miticides.
Apply neem oil or insecticidal soap as organic alternatives.
Spray undersides of leaves where mites congregate.
Rotate miticide classes to prevent resistance.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.prevention: Avoid dusty conditions around plants. Maintain adequate irrigation. Introduce predatory mites as biological control.

Tomato__Target_Spot.causes: Caused by the fungus Corynespora cassiicola. Favored by warm, humid conditions.
Tomato__Target_Spot.symptoms: Circular brown lesions with concentric rings and yellow halos on leaves, stems, and fruit.
treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil, Azoxystrobin, or Tebuconazole fungicides every 7-14 days.
Remove infected plant material.
Improve air circulation by proper staking and pruning.
Tomato__Target_Spot.prevention: Crop rotation, proper plant spacing, avoid overhead watering, remove crop debris.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.causes: Caused by Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV), transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins, stunted growth, flower drop, and severely reduced fruit set.
treatment: No cure for infected plants - remove and destroy infected plants immediately.
Control whitefly vectors with Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam, or Pymetrozine insecticides.
Apply insecticides as soil drenches or foliar sprays.
Use yellow sticky traps to monitor and reduce whitefly populations.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.prevention: Use TYLCV-resistant varieties. Apply reflective silver mulches to repel whiteflies. Use insect-proof nets in nurseries.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Caused by Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV). Spread mechanically through contaminated hands, tools, and infected seeds.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves, leaf distortion, stunted growth, and reduced fruit quality.
treatment: No chemical cure available - remove and destroy infected plants.
Disinfect tools with 10% bleach solution or 70% alcohol between plants.
Wash hands thoroughly before handling plants.
Control aphid vectors with insecticides.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Use virus-free certified seeds. Milk spray (20% skimmed milk) can provide some protection. Plant resistant varieties.

Tomato_healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms present. Leaves are dark green and healthy.
Tomato_healthy.prevention: Regular scouting, crop rotation, proper staking, balanced fertilization, and drip irrigation.

Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Caused by the fungus Venturia inaequalis. Spreads through spores in wet, cool conditions.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaves and fruit. Leaves may curl and drop early.
treatment: Apply fungicides such as Captan, Mancozeb, or Myclobutanil at bud break and every 7-10 days during wet weather.
Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruit to reduce spore load.
Prune trees to improve air circulation.
Avoid overhead irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Plant scab-resistant apple varieties. Apply dormant oil sprays before bud break.

Apple___Black_rot.causes: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa. Infects through wounds and natural openings.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown rotting lesions on fruit, purple-bordered leaf spots, and cankers on branches.
treatment: Apply Captan or Thiophanate-methyl fungicides during the growing season.
Prune out infected branches and cankers at least 15cm below visible infection.
Remove mummified fruit from trees and ground.
Sterilize pruning tools between cuts with 70% alcohol.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Maintain tree vigor through proper fertilization and watering. Remove dead wood promptly.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Caused by the fungus Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. Requires both apple and cedar/juniper trees to complete its lifecycle.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with tube-like structures on undersides.
treatment: Apply Myclobutanil, Propiconazole, or Mancozeb fungicides from pink bud stage through cover spray.
Remove nearby cedar and juniper trees if possible.
Apply fungicides every 7-10 days during spring when spores are active.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties. Avoid planting apples near cedar or juniper trees.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No disease symptoms present. Leaves are green and healthy.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Maintain regular pruning, proper fertilization, and monitor for early signs of disease.

Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5-5.5), ensure good drainage, and monitor regularly.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.causes: Caused by the fungus Podosphaera clandestina. Thrives in warm, dry conditions with high humidity.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves, shoots, and fruit. Infected leaves may curl and distort.
treatment: Apply Sulfur-based fungicides, Myclobutanil, or Potassium bicarbonate sprays.
Remove and destroy heavily infected plant material.
Apply neem oil as an organic alternative.
Ensure adequate spacing between trees for air circulation.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which promotes susceptible growth.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Regular pruning, proper irrigation, and annual fungicide program during wet seasons.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.causes: Caused by the fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis. Favored by warm, humid conditions and poor air circulation.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular grayish-tan lesions with yellow halos running parallel to leaf veins.
treatment: Apply Azoxystrobin, Propiconazole, or Pyraclostrobin fungicides at tasseling stage.
Rotate crops — avoid planting corn in the same field consecutively.
Till infected crop residue after harvest to reduce spore survival.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids. Practice crop rotation with non-host crops like soybeans.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Caused by the fungus Puccinia sorghi. Spreads rapidly via wind-blown spores in cool, moist weather.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, circular to elongated brick-red pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Apply Mancozeb, Azoxystrobin, or Trifloxystrobin fungicides early when symptoms appear.
Scout fields regularly, especially during cool wet weather.
Apply fungicide at VT/R1 growth stage for best results.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Plant resistant corn hybrids. Early planting helps avoid peak rust seasons.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Caused by the fungus Exserohilum turcicum. Favored by moderate temperatures and extended leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped gray-green to tan lesions up to 15cm on leaves.
treatment: Apply Azoxystrobin, Propiconazole, or Tebuconazole fungicides at early disease appearance.
Apply at tasseling stage for economic benefit.
Remove and destroy severely infected crop debris after harvest.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Use resistant hybrids. Practice crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Crop rotation, resistant varieties, and balanced fertilization.

Grape___Black_rot.causes: Caused by the fungus Guignardia bidwellii. Favored by warm, wet weather during early season.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with black margins, mummified black fruit (raisins on vine).
treatment: Apply Mancozeb, Myclobutanil, or Captan fungicides from bud break through veraison.
Remove and destroy all mummified fruit and infected plant material.
Apply fungicides every 10-14 days during wet weather.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Train vines to improve air circulation. Remove mummies before bud break.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).causes: Caused by a complex of fungi including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Phaeoacremonium. Enters through pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe pattern on leaves, dark streaking in wood, shriveled berries with dark spots.
treatment: No fully effective chemical cure exists. Remove and destroy severely infected vines.
Apply wound sealants (Topsin-M paste) immediately after pruning.
Double pruning technique can help manage the disease.
Apply Fosetyl-Al to reduce symptom expression.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune during dry weather. Apply wound protectants immediately after cuts. Use clean, sterilized tools.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.causes: Caused by the fungus Isariopsis clavispora (Pseudocercospora vitis). Thrives in warm, humid conditions.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Angular dark brown spots on leaves, often near margins. Premature defoliation in severe cases.
treatment: Apply Mancozeb, Copper hydroxide, or Captan fungicides.
Remove infected leaves and improve canopy management.
Apply fungicides every 10-14 days during humid weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Maintain open canopy through proper pruning. Avoid excessive nitrogen.

Grape___healthy.prevention: Regular canopy management, proper trellising, and seasonal fungicide program.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).causes: Caused by the bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, spread by the Asian citrus psyllid insect.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Yellow mottling of leaves (blotchy mottle), lopsided bitter fruit, twig dieback, and stunted growth.
treatment: No cure exists - infected trees should be removed and destroyed to prevent spread.
Control psyllid populations with Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam, or Spinosad insecticides.
Apply foliar nutritional sprays to extend productive life of mildly infected trees.
Thermotherapy (heat treatment) shows some promise but is not widely available.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material. Install psyllid monitoring traps. Apply systemic insecticides to control vector.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos. Cracking and pitting on fruit.
treatment: Apply Copper hydroxide or Copper sulfate bactericides during the growing season.
Apply Oxytetracycline (where registered) at petal fall and shuck split.
Avoid working in orchards when wet to reduce spread.
Remove and destroy heavily infected plant material.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation. Apply copper sprays preventively.

Peach___healthy.prevention: Annual pruning, proper thinning, and preventive copper sprays in spring.
